rationale: I5 instrument: Interest/Enjoyment subscale of the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory. I6 Results: "Intrinsic motivation scores, as measured by the Interest/Enjoyment subscale of the IMI, were as follows: control group (mean 26.06, SD 1.87), Kinect group (mean 35.13, SD 3.20)". Randomized 3-arm trial with video-guided exercise control; exergame scores movement accuracy. Duration per Abstract: "Participants engaged in a 10-minute intervention once per week for 7 weeks".
doubt: I4: the Abstract says 7 weeks, but Methods say "Participants were then instructed to continue the 10-minute intervention daily for 7 consecutive days" and refer to a "1-week period"; the paper contradicts itself on scheduled length. IMI was measured after the first session and possibly not at the end of the programme. Also I3: the control arm is video-guided exercise, not an exergame.

rationale: Abstract/Methods: "Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 4th week and 8th week assesment using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Visual Analog Scale (VAS)" - pain, disability and pelvic floor instruments only; motivation appears only as background in the abstract.

Introduction: "the present study measured behavioural outcomes only and did not assess flow, enjoyment, or cognitive load directly"; outcomes were concentration, reaction time, flexibility and balance.

criterion: E6: No motivation results by arm
rationale: Methods name BREQ-2 as a measure, but Results give a single group value: "The RAI score is 15.79±3.80" and "high level of motivation" for "motor behavior towards VR"; no BREQ-2 result is given for the conventional-training control arm.
doubt: E6: the text does not say outright that BREQ-2 was given only to the VR group; I judged it from the single reported value and the supplementary table label.

rationale: Intervention: "The intervention utilized two commercially available mobile applications—MyFitnessPal and 7-Minute Workout" - an exercise-logging app and a video-guided circuit app, with no movement-controlled game. No motivation instrument either (motivation only from interviews).
doubt: E1: the paper calls the intervention "exergaming and virtual reality" but describes only fitness apps; the criterion leaves open whether to go by the authors' label or the described intervention.
